---

The official Kotlin library for the Tungo Platform API (`https://api.tungo.kz`): the AI accountant, 1C integration, bank statements, e-invoices, tax forms and automations of [Tungo AI](https://tungo.kz).

It is generated from the API's OpenAPI contract, so its methods and models always match the contract it was built from.

## Requirements

Kotlin 2.0 or newer on JVM 8 or newer; the library is compiled to Java 8 bytecode and uses only Java 8 APIs, so it also works on Android (API 21+). It depends on OkHttp 4.12.0, kotlinx-coroutines 1.9.0 and kotlinx-serialization-json 1.7.3. Every operation is a suspending function; call it from a coroutine.

## Installation

Gradle (Kotlin DSL):

```kotlin
dependencies {
    implementation("kz.tungo:tungo-sdk-kotlin:0.2.0")
}
```

Maven:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>kz.tungo</groupId>
  <artifactId>tungo-sdk-kotlin</artifactId>
  <version>0.2.0</version>
</dependency>
```

## Quick start

```kotlin
import kz.tungo.sdk.kotlin.TungoClient
import kz.tungo.sdk.kotlin.resources.ask

suspend fun main() {
    // The API key is read from the environment variable TUNGO_API_KEY.
    val client = TungoClient()

    val companies = client.companies.list()
    for (company in companies.data) println("${company.id} ${company.name}")

    val turn = client.chat.ask("Какой НДС к уплате за октябрь?", companyId = companies.data.first().id)
    println(turn.answer)

    client.close()
}
```

## Authentication and configuration

Create one client and share it: it is immutable and safe to use from several threads or tasks. Every option can be passed explicitly; five of them fall back to environment variables.

| Option | Environment variable | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key | `TUNGO_API_KEY` | none |
| Base URL | `TUNGO_BASE_URL` | `https://api.tungo.kz` |
| Webhook secret | `TUNGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | none |
| Default company | `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID` | none |
| Default workspace | `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID` | none |
| Timeout | | 60 s (600 s for non-streaming chat turns) |
| Maximum retries | | 2 |
| Default headers, HTTP client | | none, built-in |

The API key is sent only to operations that require it; public endpoints and incoming hooks never receive it, and it never appears in error messages or debug output. Calling an authenticated operation without a key fails locally, before any request is made.

Every method also accepts per-request options: timeout, maximum retries, extra headers, an idempotency key and cancellation.

```kotlin
val client = TungoClient {
    apiKey = System.getenv("MY_TUNGO_KEY")
    baseUrl = "https://api.tungo.kz"
    webhookSecret = System.getenv("MY_WEBHOOK_SECRET")
    companyId = "co_01h455vb4pex5vsknk084sn02q" // default for company-scoped calls
    timeout = 30.seconds
    maxRetries = 3
    header("X-Client", "billing-service")
    httpClient = OkHttpClient.Builder().proxy(Proxy(Proxy.Type.HTTP, InetSocketAddress("proxy.local", 3128))).build()
}

// Options of one request. A call is cancelled by cancelling its coroutine.
val company = client.companies.get(
    requestOptions = RequestOptions {
        timeout = 5.seconds
        maxRetries = 0
        header("X-Trace-Id", "trace-42")
    },
)
println(company.name)

// A copy of the client with some options changed; it shares the connection pool.
val patient = client.withOptions { timeout = 2.minutes }
println(patient.options.timeout)

// Status, headers, request id and rate limit of one call.
val response = client.companies.withRawResponse.list()
println("${response.status} ${response.requestId} ${response.rateLimit?.remaining}")
```

Company-scoped and workspace-scoped methods take `companyId` / `workspaceId`; when the argument is omitted the default of the client is used (`companyId`, `workspaceId` options or the environment variables `TUNGO_COMPANY_ID`, `TUNGO_WORKSPACE_ID`). A supplied `OkHttpClient` contributes its connection pool, proxy, interceptors and TLS settings; the SDK applies its own timeouts on top of it and does not shut it down in `close()`.

## Errors

Every failure is a subtype of the SDK's base error. An HTTP error response becomes an API error chosen by the `error.type` field of the response body, falling back to the HTTP status when the body is not the API's error envelope:

| `error.type` | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_request_error` | 400 |
| `authentication_error` | 401 |
| `payment_required_error` | 402 |
| `permission_error` | 403 |
| `not_found_error` | 404 |
| `conflict_error` | 409 |
| `gone_error` | 410 |
| `limit_error` | 429 |
| `api_error` | 500 |
| `unavailable_error` | 503 |

An API error carries the status, type, code, message, request id, field errors, the parsed retry-after delay, the response headers and the raw body. Problems that happen without a response have their own types: connection error, timeout, decode error (a successful response whose body is not valid), and configuration or validation error (raised before any request).

```kotlin
try {
    client.proposals.approve("P-000042")
} catch (e: NotFoundException) {
    println("No such proposal (request ${e.requestId})")
} catch (e: LimitException) {
    println("Slow down; retry after ${e.retryAfter}")
} catch (e: TungoApiException) {
    println("${e.status} ${e.type} ${e.code}: ${e.apiMessage}")
    for (field in e.fields) println("${field.path}: ${field.message}")
} catch (e: TungoTimeoutException) {
    println("Timed out: ${e.message}")
} catch (e: TungoConnectionException) {
    println("Network problem: ${e.message}")
} catch (e: TungoException) {
    println("Other SDK failure: ${e.message}")
}
```

The base class is `TungoException`. API errors are `TungoApiException` and its subclasses `InvalidRequestException`, `AuthenticationException`, `PaymentRequiredException`, `PermissionDeniedException`, `NotFoundException`, `ConflictException`, `GoneException`, `LimitException`, `InternalServerException` and `ServiceUnavailableException`. Local failures are `TungoConnectionException`, `TungoTimeoutException` (an HTTP attempt ran out of time) with its subclass `TungoWaitTimeoutException` (the deadline of a waiting helper passed; no request failed), `TungoDecodeException`, `TungoConfigException`, `TungoValidationException`, `TungoPaginationException` and `WebhookVerificationException`. Cancellation is never wrapped: a cancelled call throws `CancellationException` as usual.

## Retries and timeouts

A request is retried up to 2 times (3 attempts) on connection errors, timeouts and the statuses 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 and 504, but only when repeating it is safe: `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT` and `DELETE` requests, and `POST` or `PATCH` requests of the operations whose contract declares an `Idempotency-Key`. For those the SDK generates a random key and reuses it for every attempt; you can pass your own. Other operations send no key, not even one you pass, because the API would ignore it.

The delay between attempts is `min(0.5 s × 2^attempt, 8 s)` with random jitter. A positive `retry-after-ms` or `Retry-After` response header overrides it; if the server asks for more than 60 s the SDK does not wait and raises the error with the delay filled in.

The timeout covers the whole request including reading the body. Streaming calls have no total timeout, only a connect timeout and an idle timeout of 120 s. Cancellation supplied by the caller is combined with the timeout.

```kotlin
// For the whole client.
val client = TungoClient {
    maxRetries = 5
    timeout = 20.seconds
}

// For one request, with your own idempotency key.
val job = client.batches.createEsfPurchases(
    requestOptions = RequestOptions {
        maxRetries = 1
        timeout = 2.minutes
        idempotencyKey = "esf-2026-11-09"
    },
)
println(job.id)
```

A `Retry-After` (or `retry-after-ms`) of the server is honoured when it asks for a positive delay of at most 60 s; zero, a negative number or a date in the past means the computed backoff, never an immediate retry. The connect timeout is 30 s by default (`connectTimeout`), separate from the timeout of an attempt.

## Pagination

List operations use cursor pagination (`{ data, next_cursor }`). The plain method returns one typed page that knows whether there is a next page and can fetch it. The auto-paging variant is a lazy iterator: it requests the next page only when needed, carries your filters over, and stops fetching as soon as you stop iterating.

```kotlin
// One page at a time.
var page: Page<ProposalListItem, ProposalPage>? = client.proposals.list(limit = 50, status = "draft")
while (page != null) {
    for (proposal in page.data) println(proposal.id)
    page = page.next()
}

// Every item as a cold Flow: pages are requested while you collect.
client.proposals.listAll(status = "draft")
    .take(120)
    .collect { proposal -> println(proposal.id) }
```

A page is `Page<Item, Response>`: `data`, `nextCursor`, `hasNext`, `next()`, and `body` / `response` for the rest of the response. The `...All` functions return a cold `Flow`. A cursor that comes back a second time while paging (the server sends A, B and then A again) stops the iteration with `TungoPaginationException` instead of looping forever.

## Streaming

Streaming operations use server-sent events and deliver typed events as they arrive. Leaving the loop early or closing the stream closes the connection. A stream request is retried only before its first byte; an error response is raised as the same typed API error as for ordinary calls. A chat stream that ends before its final event is reported as an error, never as a finished answer.

```kotlin
// A cold Flow of typed events; cancelling the collection closes the connection.
client.chat.createStream(ChatMessageRequest(message = "Сколько НДС к уплате за октябрь?")).collect { event ->
    when (event) {
        is ChatEventText -> print(event.delta)
        is ChatEventTool -> println("[tool ${event.name}: ${event.status}]")
        is ChatEventError -> println("error: ${event.error.message}")
        is ChatEventDone -> println("\nstop reason: ${event.stopReason}")
        else -> Unit
    }
}

// Or let the SDK put the answer together. An error event of the turn is thrown as a TungoApiException,
// a stream that ends before its done event as a TungoDecodeException.
val turn = client.chat.streamTurn(ChatMessageRequest(message = "А за ноябрь?")) { event ->
    if (event is ChatEventText) print(event.delta)
}
println("dialog ${turn.dialogId}, turn ${turn.turnNo}: ${turn.text}")
```

Unknown event types are delivered as `ChatEvent.Unknown` instead of failing. `withRawResponse.createStream(...) { stream -> ... }` gives the response headers together with the events; `stream.dialogId` and `stream.turnNo` read `X-Dialog-Id` and `X-Turn-No`.

- The flow is cold: every collection sends the request again. For an operation with an idempotency key (`createStream`) the key is fixed when the flow is created, so collecting the same flow twice repeats the same turn instead of starting a second one; call the function again for a new turn.
- A turn is finished only by its `done` event. When the stream ends without it (a cut connection, for example), `streamTurn` and `accumulate` throw `TungoDecodeException` instead of returning the partial text; collecting the raw flow simply ends, and `ChatStreamAccumulator.isComplete` tells the two cases apart.
- Every error event of a turn makes `streamTurn` and `accumulate` throw a `TungoApiException`, also when its data is not in the shape of the contract (the raw flow delivers such an event as `ChatEvent.Unknown` with the type `error`).
- A successful reply that is not `text/event-stream` (JSON, the HTML page of a proxy) is a `TungoDecodeException`, not an empty stream.
- The feed stream (`feed.listEvents`) decodes the events named `feed`; an event named `error` ends the flow with a `TungoApiException` carrying its code and message, and events of other names are skipped.

## Webhooks

Outgoing webhooks are signed according to the Standard Webhooks specification (Svix). The verify helper takes the raw request body and the headers (`webhook-*` or `svix-*`), checks the HMAC-SHA256 signature in constant time and the timestamp within 300 s of the system clock, and returns the typed event. Any problem is reported as a webhook verification error. If no secret is passed, the client's webhook secret is used.

The send-hook helper posts an event to an incoming hook (`/hooks/{token}`) and, when given a secret, signs the exact bytes it sends in the `X-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header. The API key is never sent to hooks.

```kotlin
// In your HTTP handler: the raw body and the request headers.
fun handle(client: TungoClient, rawBody: String, headers: Map<String, String>) {
    val event = try {
        client.verifyWebhook(rawBody, headers) // uses the webhook secret of the client
    } catch (e: WebhookVerificationException) {
        println("Rejected: ${e.reason}")
        return
    }
    when (event) {
        is WebhookEventProposalWritten -> println("written: ${event.data}")
        is WebhookEvent.Unknown -> println("unknown event type ${event.type}")
        else -> println(event.type)
    }
}

// Sending an event to an incoming hook, signed with the hook secret.
suspend fun send(client: TungoClient) {
    val accepted = client.sendHook(
        token = "hk_live_token",
        payload = """{"id":"order_1532","amount_tiyn":4500000}""",
        secret = "hook-signing-secret",
        eventId = "order_1532",
    )
    println(accepted)
}
```

## Money

The API expresses amounts in tiyn (1/100 of a tenge) as 64-bit integers. The money helper converts decimal strings and exact decimal values to tiyn without floating-point error, rounding half away from zero (`"1.005"` → `101`), and formats tiyn for display (`4500000` → `45 000,00 ₸`). Invalid input raises a typed error.

```kotlin
val tiyn: Long = TungoMoney.toTiyn("45000.50")      // 4500050
println(TungoMoney.toTiyn("1.005"))                 // 101
println(TungoMoney.formatTiyn(tiyn))                // 45 000,50 ₸
println(TungoMoney.formatTiyn(123456, "USD"))       // 1 234,56 $
println(TungoMoney.isValidBinIin("990140000017"))
```

`toTiyn` also accepts `BigDecimal`. The `Double` overload converts through the shortest decimal representation of the number.

## Models

Requests and responses are `@Serializable` data classes in `kz.tungo.sdk.kotlin.models`. Decoding is strict about the contract and tolerant of additions: an unknown property, a new enum value, a new variant of a union and a `null` or missing optional property never fail; a missing required property or a value of the wrong JSON type (a number where a string is expected, a fraction where an integer is expected) fails the call with `TungoDecodeException`, which keeps the status, the headers and the body. One leniency of kotlinx-serialization remains: a number sent in quotes is accepted for a numeric property. Enumerations are open: an enum is a value class over the wire value with a constant per known value, so a value added by the API later is kept (`isKnown` is false) instead of failing. Tagged unions (stream events, webhook events) are sealed interfaces with an `Unknown` variant that keeps the raw JSON; it is used for a tag this version does not know and for a payload that does not match the contract, so one odd event never fails a stream. Other unions are value classes over `JsonElement` with typed accessors (`asString()`, `asBoolean()`, ...). 64-bit integers are `Long`; dates stay RFC 3339 strings.

Compatibility: the models are data classes, and the API adds properties over time. A new optional property is source-compatible for code that names its arguments, but it changes the constructor, `copy` and `componentN` of the class, so it is not binary-compatible and it shifts positional destructuring. Construct models with named arguments, do not destructure them, and recompile against a new version of the SDK instead of swapping the jar; the public API of every release is recorded in `api/tungo-sdk-kotlin.api`.

Where the API distinguishes a missing property from `null` in a request, the property has the type `NullableField`:

```kotlin
client.webhooks.updateEndpoint("ep_1", WebhookEndpointPatch(channels = NullableField.Null))                 // clear
client.webhooks.updateEndpoint("ep_1", WebhookEndpointPatch(channels = NullableField.of(listOf("billing")))) // set
client.webhooks.updateEndpoint("ep_1", WebhookEndpointPatch(enabled = false))                                // leave channels as they are
```

## Long-running operations

Helpers poll until a job reaches a final state, with an interval growing from 1 s to 5 s and an overall deadline; when the deadline passes they throw `TungoWaitTimeoutException` (a subclass of `TungoTimeoutException`, so existing handlers keep working; nothing is cancelled on the server).

```kotlin
val run = client.automations.runScenarioAndWait("sc_1", timeout = 5.minutes)
println("${run.state}: ${run.answer}")

val job = client.batches.waitForBatch("job_1")
println(job.running)
```

## API reference

Generated from the Tungo Platform API contract: **13 resources, 82 methods, 22 webhook event types**.

| Resource | Description | Methods |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `client.workspaces` | Organisations (workspaces) the API key can access | `list` |
| `client.companies` | Companies of an organisation and their profiles | `list` · `get` |
| `client.platform` | Platform balance, ledger, usage reports, limits, audit log and model rates | `listUsageRates` · `getAccount` · `getAudit / getAuditAll` · `getLedger / getLedgerAll` · `listLimits` · `listRequests / listRequestsAll` · `getUsage` |
| `client.apiKeys` | The current API key and its usage statistics | `getCurrent` · `getCurrentUsage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.webhooks` | Outgoing webhooks of an organisation (Svix): endpoints, event catalogue, deliveries and signature check | `listEndpoints / listEndpointsAll` · `createEndpoint` · `getEndpoint` · `updateEndpoint` · `deleteEndpoint` · `listEndpointAttempts / listEndpointAttemptsAll` · `rotateEndpointSecret` · `testEndpoint` · `listEventTypes` · `listMessages / listMessagesAll` · `listMessageAttempts / listMessageAttemptsAll` · `resendMessage` · `getUsage` |
| `client.chat` | Conversations with the AI accountant: questions, streaming chat (SSE), token counting and history | `list / listAll` · `create / createStream` · `countTokens` · `get` · `update` · `delete` · `answer / answerStream` · `listEvents` · `stop` |
| `client.proposals` | Documents proposed by the AI accountant: review, approval for posting to 1C, and rejection | `list / listAll` · `approveBatch` · `get` · `approve` · `reject` |
| `client.feed` | The company's feed of events and proposals (pages and a live SSE stream) | `get / getAll` · `listEvents` |
| `client.batches` | Processing batches for bank statements, incoming e-invoices and DirectBank | `list / listAll` · `createBankStatement` · `createEsfPurchases` · `get` · `listEvents` · `stop` · `getSummary` · `listStatements / listStatementsAll` · `pollDirectbank` |
| `client.esf` | Incoming and outgoing electronic invoices (the ESF system) | `getIncoming / getIncomingAll` · `getOutgoing / getOutgoingAll` |
| `client.forms` | Tax forms (FNO 100.00 and others): building, ISNA checks and data gaps | `list` · `build` · `listDataGaps` · `getIsna` · `listNotes` |
| `client.onec` | Status of the company's connection to its 1C database | `getStatus` |
| `client.automations` | Company automations: incoming hooks, scenarios, step chains, runs and the AI autonomy level | `postHook` · `listHooks` · `createHook` · `getHook` · `updateHook` · `deleteHook` · `rotateHook` · `testHook` · `listRuns / listRunsAll` · `getRun` · `cancelRun` · `retryRun` · `listScenarios` · `createScenario` · `getScenario` · `putScenario` · `updateScenario` · `deleteScenario` · `runScenario` · `getState` · `putState` · `getAutonomy` · `putAutonomy` |

## Versioning and support

This library follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). While the major version is 0, a minor release may contain breaking changes; they are always listed in the [changelog](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-kotlin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). This README describes version 0.2.0.

The code is generated: please report problems and ideas in the [issue tracker](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-kotlin/issues) rather than opening pull requests against generated files. To report a vulnerability, follow the [security policy](https://github.com/TungoAI/tungo-sdk-kotlin/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
